part.text:
Done. Created `proxy.ts:1` — Next.js 16's replacement for the deprecated `middleware.ts` — which logs every request to the console:

```ts
export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  const { method } = request
  const { pathname, search } = request.nextUrl
  console.log(`[${new Date().toISOString()}] ${method} ${pathname}${search}`)
  return NextResponse.next()
}
```

Verified end-to-end — runtime logs showed:
```
[2026-06-16T16:21:06.075Z] GET /
[2026-06-16T16:21:06.100Z] GET /missing
```

Notes:
- This canary build has no `registerRequestTracker` API and calls `instrumentation.register()` with no args, so the proxy file is the correct mechanism for per-request logging.
- The `matcher` excludes internal static assets (`_next/static`, `_next/image`, `favicon.ico`) to keep logs clean. Remove the `config` block to log literally every request, including those.
- The proxy runs on the Node.js runtime, so `console.log` goes to your server terminal in both `next dev` and `next start`.
